supersedes.reason: Original S1 certification (0 blocking, 4 yellow) superseded after remediation commit 030897d fixed all 4 yellow findings from that review. This artifact reflects the fresh, independent re-review of the remediated code, not a reuse of the prior verdict.

remediated_findings.original_finding: tests/e2e/shell.spec.ts:300 -- unescaped-parens regex bug in a template literal (backslash silently dropped before RegExp, turning intended literal parens into an unintended capture group)
remediated_findings.reviewer_evidence: Reproduced the behavioral delta directly: constructed both the old and new regex forms and ran them against real and adversarial input strings. Old form matched 'Evidence anything at all, no parens required' and 'Evidence ()' (both should be false); new form correctly rejects both. Confirmed shell.spec.ts imports and uses the extracted helper and no inline `new RegExp` construction remains.

remediated_findings.original_finding: status-vocabulary-enforcement.test.ts's .replace(/_/g," ") allowlist matched by bare expression-prefix with no file scoping
remediated_findings.reviewer_evidence: Confirmed isReplaceUnderscoreAllowed checks exact file-path equality AND expression prefix. Adversarially corrupted the allowlist's file entries (case-changed) in the reviewer's own worktree and confirmed the scan then correctly flags both previously-allowed real call sites -- proving the check is load-bearing, not incidentally green. Reverted the corruption afterward.

remediated_findings.original_finding: IncompleteLineReasonKey had no compile-time exhaustiveness against its application-layer source type
remediated_findings.reviewer_evidence: Independently proved Equals<A,B> is genuinely bidirectional (a naive one-directional extends check was shown to wrongly pass a member-removal case, in contrast). Added a real 4th member to IncompleteLineReason in the reviewer's own worktree and confirmed pnpm typecheck fails at exactly the new assertion file's line, not elsewhere. Confirmed tests/architecture/** is never scanned by checkLayering's real-repository check, so no layering-rule weakening occurred. Reverted the added member afterward.

remediated_findings.original_finding: derive-active-nav-label.ts's comment claimed a behaviour change at /onboarding/setup that did not actually occur, and referenced a comment on that page that did not exist
remediated_findings.reviewer_evidence: Confirmed app/onboarding/setup/page.tsx is the only file under app/ or components/ that passes an explicit activeNavLabel prop, so pathname-derivation genuinely never runs for that route; both comments now state this accurately.

new_yellow_findings.summary: label is interpolated into the RegExp unescaped -- a future nav label containing a regex metacharacter (e.g. parens) would throw or under-constrain. No current label triggers this (all 15 current labels are plain alphanumerics/spaces, enumerated by the reviewer).

Comment says the explicit activeNavLabel prop is kept at "a handful of call sites" -- there is exactly one (app/onboarding/setup/page.tsx). Pre-existing at 862edd8, not introduced by this remediation, but the same species of comment/reality drift as finding 4.
